news.title: Accidental Payment Scam: Don't Send Money Back
news.excerpt:
You get an unexpected payment — Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a text
message says someone sent you money by mistake. Then a message follows:
"They accidentally sent you money, please send it back." If you send it
back, you lose. The original payment may be fraudulent and get reversed
by the bank, but the money you voluntarily sent is gone for good.

What to do: Do not send money back. Leave the funds untouched and
contact your bank or payment service through its official app, website,
or customer-service number. Do not trust screenshots or messages from
the sender as proof. Avoid clicking links from strangers — they lead to
fake login pages.

This matters: Scammers use stolen cards or hacked accounts to send the
initial payment. When the real owner disputes it, the bank reverses...

news.title: CISA adds four new actively exploited vulnerabilities to catalog — patch GPUStack, FreeSwitch, OpenSSH, Aspera now
news.excerpt: CISA added four new actively exploited vulnerabilities on November 9: GPUStack (CVE-2026-102895), SignalWire FreeSwitch (CVE-2026-116779), OpenBSD OpenSSH (CVE-2026-123158), and IBM Aspera Faspex (CVE-2026-123218). Check the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog at cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog and update any affected software immediately.

news.title: AI Voice Clone Scams Are Calling — Hang Up and Call Back on a Known Number
news.excerpt:
AI voice clone scams are calling people right now. The caller sounds exactly like a family member — a grandchild, a child, a spouse — and says they're in trouble. They need money immediately for bail, a car repair, a medical emergency. It's not them. Scammers use AI to clone voices from social media videos.

The call feels real because the voice is real — it's a copy of someone you love. The scammer pressures you to act fast, send money, don't tell anyone.

What to do: Hang up. Call the person back on a number you know is theirs. If you can't reach them, call another family member to check. Never send money or gift cards based on a surprise call, no matter how real the voice sounds.

news.title: Holiday Shopping Scams Hide in Your Search Results
news.excerpt:
Holiday shopping scams are hiding at the top of your search results.

When you search for a gift, the first links are often paid ads from scammers — not the real store. Click one and you could hand over your credit card or personal information to a fake site that looks almost identical to the real thing.

What to do: Scroll past the top results. The organic listings below the ads are ranked by relevance, not by who paid the most. Better yet, type the store's web address directly into your browser. If you're not sure about a site, search the company name plus "complaint" or "scam" before you buy.

news.title: Fake Jury Duty Calls Targeting North Florida — Hang Up
news.excerpt:
Scammers are calling people in North Florida pretending to be court officials. They claim you missed jury duty and owe a fine. They demand immediate payment by gift card or wire transfer. Courts never call to demand money — they send official mail. If you get this call, hang up. Do not provide any personal information or payment.

What to do: If you're unsure whether you have a real court obligation, look up the official clerk of court phone number yourself and call them. Never use a number the caller gives you. Report the scam call to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

posts.title: CISA warns SharePoint servers under active attack — patch CVE-2026-65660 and CVE-2026-67279 now
posts.summary: Apply the November 2026 Microsoft security update via Windows Update or the Microsoft Update Catalog — it patches the actively exploited SharePoint code injection and SSH workflow flaws.

posts.title: Firefox 160 blocks sites from hijacking your email links — new mailto permission control free at firefox.com
posts.summary: Update to Firefox 160 at firefox.com or Settings > General > Firefox Updates — the mailto block setting is in Privacy & Security > Applications > mailto.
posts.truth: I see so many customers who accidentally set some random site as their default email handler — this stops that cold.

posts.title: Windows 11 26H2 brings Hotpatch updates — security patches without restart for Enterprise at microsoft.com
posts.summary: Check Settings > Windows Update for the 26H2 enablement package — Hotpatch requires Enterprise edition and the latest baseline cumulative update (KB5121794 or later).
posts.truth: Most home users don't need Hotpatch, but if you run a business that can't afford downtime, this is the feature to upgrade for.

posts.title: Clay Electric outage texts tell you the power is out before your neighbor knows — free at clayelectric.com
posts.summary: Sign up at clayelectric.com > MyClayElectric or text OUT to 855-939-3840 for real-time outage alerts to your phone.
posts.truth: Around here, the power flickers and people wonder if it's just them — this tells you instantly and lets you report it without calling.

posts.title: Ventoy puts every ISO on one USB — free multi-boot tool at ventoy.net beats reformatting every time
posts.summary: Download Ventoy at ventoy.net, run it on your USB drive, then drag and drop ISO files — no reformatting needed.
posts.truth: I used to carry a bag of USB drives for every Windows version and Linux distro — now one Ventoy drive does it all.

posts.title: Windows 11 November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,252 vulnerabilities including an exploited zero-day
posts.summary: Install KB5132061 from Windows Update (Settings > Windows Update) — it patches 68 critical flaws and one actively exploited zero-day in Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2. Supported versions get build 26300.9974 (26H2), 26200.9974 (25H2), or 26100.9974 (24H2 Enterprise/Education).
posts.truth: Most people ignore updates until something breaks. I see it every week — a computer comes in with a problem that a patch from two months ago would have prevented. The zero-day in this release is already being used in attacks. Don't wait.

posts.title: Comcast Xfinity fiber expands to 3300 more Columbia County homes and businesses with 2000 more by year end
posts.summary: Comcast announced August 25 that Xfinity fiber-powered internet now reaches over 3,300 homes and businesses in Columbia County, with construction ongoing to add 2,000 more locations by end of 2026. Check if your Lake City address qualifies at xfinity.com — enter your address to see available plans and speeds.

posts.title: Firefox 160 Mini Window pops any tab into an always-on-top overlay for multitasking free
posts.summary: Firefox 160 (released November 10) adds Mini Window — right-click any tab and choose Open in Mini Window to keep a video, document, or page visible while you work in other apps. Also new: Picture-in-Picture playback speed controls (0.25x–2x), a "Never Allow" button to stop sites from pestering you to handle email links, and on-device speech recognition in 40 languages. Update free at firefox.com or Menu > Help > About Firefox.

posts.title: Windows 11 November 2026 update brings Hotpatch security updates and Cloud Rebuild free
posts.summary: The November 2026 update (KB5132061) for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 includes Hotpatch support — security updates that install without a restart — and Cloud Rebuild, which lets you reinstall Windows from the cloud without a USB drive. Get it now: open Settings > Windows Update and click Check for updates.
